g.text: 180° phase relationship across a center-tapped winding

text.style: font-size: 12px; font-family: 'Inter', 'system-ui', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: middle; fill: #444444

g.text: Two ends of a CT winding are exact mirror images relative to the CT — when one is +V, the other is −V.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'system-ui', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: middle; fill: #555555

g.text: Whichever lead is positive drives its 5AR4 anode into conduction.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'system-ui', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: middle; fill: #555555

g.text: The same trick reappears in phase splitters and push-pull output transformers.
